rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah had called his people persistently by night and day, openly and privately, but each repeated call met hardened unbelief and resistance.
rows.anchor: لما طال مقام نبي الله بين أظهرهم يدعوهم إلى الله ليلا ونهارا، وجهرا وإسرارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people threatened to stone Noah if he stopped summoning them to his religion.
rows.anchor: أي: عن دعوتك إيانا إلى دينك يا نوح

words: فافتَح بيني وبينهم فتحا ونجني ومن معي من المؤمنين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the threat, Noah prayed for judgment between him and his deniers and for the rescue of himself and the believers with him; God answered.
rows.anchor: فعند ذلك دعا عليهم دعوة استجاب الله منه، فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah's plea is paralleled by his prayer and the flood account in 54:10–14.
rows.anchor: كما قال في الآية الأخرى: {فدعا ربه أني مغلوب فانتصر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The loaded ark was full of provisions and the pairs carried aboard; Noah and all who accompanied him were saved, while all who denied and disobeyed him drowned, making the event a sign though most did not believe.
rows.anchor: والمشحون: هو المملوء بالأمتعة والأزواج التي حمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God drowned all the rest who denied Noah, and the episode is a sign; most remained unbelievers, while God is Mighty and Merciful.
rows.anchor: وأغرقنا من كذبه وخالف أمره كلهم، {إن في ذلك لآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣāliḥ was God's servant and messenger, sent to the Arab people of Thamūd, who lived at al-Ḥijr between Wādī al-Qurā and Syria.
rows.anchor: بعثه إلى قوم ثمود، وكانوا عربا يسكنون مدينة الحجر، التي بين وادي القرى وبلاد الشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet passed by Thamūd while heading on a campaign toward Syria, reached Tabūk, then returned to Medina to prepare for it.
rows.anchor: الأحاديث المروية في مرور رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamūd came after ʿĀd and before Abraham; Ṣāliḥ called them to worship God alone and obey the message, but they rejected and opposed him.
rows.anchor: وقد كانوا بعد عاد وقبل الخليل، عليه السلام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣāliḥ sought no wage from them for his call; he sought its reward only from God and then reminded them of God's favors.
rows.anchor: أنه لا يبتغي بدعوتهم أجرا منهم، وإنما يطلب ثواب ذلك من الله، عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lūṭ was Lūṭ son of Hārān son of Āzar, Abraham's nephew.
rows.anchor: لوط بن هاران بن آزر، وهو ابن أخي إبراهيم الخليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent Lūṭ to a great people during Abraham's lifetime; they lived in Sodom and its environs, later made into a foul lake in al-Ghawr near Jerusalem and between al-Karak and al-Shawbak.
rows.anchor: في حياة إبراهيم، وكانوا يسكنون "سدوم" وأعمالها التي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lūṭ called his people to worship God alone, obey the messenger sent to them, and avoid disobeying God.
rows.anchor: فدعاهم إلى الله، عز وجل، أن يعبدوه وحده لا شريك له، وأن يطيعوا رسولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lūṭ forbade their unprecedented sexual transgression: approaching males instead of the women God created for them.
rows.anchor: ونهاهم عن معصية الله، وارتكاب ما كانوا قد ابتدعوه في العالم، مما لم يسبقهم الخلائق إلى فعله

words: وَتَذَرُونَ مَا خَلَقَ لَكُمْ رَبُّكُم مِّنْ أَزْوَٰجِكُم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Lūṭ forbade their lewd approach to males and directed them to their wives, they threatened expulsion unless he stopped preaching.
rows.anchor: لما نهاهم نبي الله عن إتيانهم الفواحش، وغشيانهم الذكور، وأرشدهم إلى إتيان نسائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat meant that they would drive Lūṭ out from among them.
rows.anchor: يعنون: عما جئتنا (1) به، {لتكونن من المخرجين}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their threat echoes the people's response in 7:82: to expel Lūṭ and his followers because they claimed to be pure.
rows.anchor: كما قال تعالى: {وما (2) كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lūṭ described himself as hating their act: he neither loved nor approved it and therefore disavowed them.
rows.anchor: أي: المبغضين، لا أحبه ولا أرضى به؛ فأنا بريء منكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lūṭ prayed for rescue from their deeds, and God saved his entire household.
rows.anchor: قال: {رب نجني وأهلي مما يعملون}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The old woman left among those who perished was Lūṭ's wicked wife.
rows.anchor: وهي امرأته، وكانت عجوز سوء بقيت فهلكت (4) مع من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As also recounted in al-Aʿrāf, Hūd, and al-Ḥijr, God ordered Lūṭ to leave by night with his family except his wife and not turn at the cry; the others were universally destroyed by a shower of layered sijjīl stones.
rows.anchor: حين أمره الله أن يسري بأهله إلا امرأته، وأنهم لا يلتفتون إذا سمعوا الصيحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destruction is a sign; most people did not believe, and God is Mighty and Merciful.
rows.anchor: إن في ذلك لآية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين. وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم

words: فَلَا تَدْعُ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا ءَاخَرَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands worship of Him alone and states that He punishes whoever associates another deity with Him.
rows.anchor: آمرا بعبادته وحده لا شريك له، ومخبرا أن من أشرك به عذبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger must warn his nearest relatives; no one among them is exempt from the need for faith in God.
rows.anchor: أن ينذر عشيرته الأقربين، أي: الأدنين إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He is to be gentle toward the believers who follow him and disavow any creature who disobeys, whoever that may be.
rows.anchor: أن يلين جانبه لمن اتبعه من عباد الله المؤمنين. ومن عصاه من خلق الله كائنا من كان فليتبرأ منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This special warning is one part of the general warning, not a contradiction; Ibn Kathīr links it to the warnings in 36:6, 42:7, 6:51, 19:97, 6:19, and 11:17.
rows.anchor: وهذه النذارة الخاصة لا تنافي العامة، بل هي فرد من أجزائها، كما قال: {لتنذر قوما ما أنذر آباؤهم فهم غافلون}

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: In Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, the Prophet swears that any Jew or Christian of this community who hears of him and does not believe will enter the Fire.
rows.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم: "والذي نفسي بيده، لا يسمع بي أحد من هذه الأمة، يهودي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that after the verse was revealed, the Prophet called the clans at Ṣafā, asked if they would believe news of cavalry preparing to raid, then warned of severe punishment; Abū Lahab cursed him and 111:1 was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس قال: لما أنزل الله، عز وجل:

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that the Prophet publicly warned Fāṭima, Ṣafiyya, and Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib that he could not protect them before God, though they could ask for his wealth; Muslim alone transmits it.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام أحمد: حدثنا وكيع، حدثنا هشام، عن أبيه

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that the Prophet called Quraysh and successive clans to save themselves from the Fire, including Fāṭima, whom he could not save though he would maintain kinship.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه، قال: لما نزلت هذه الآية:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhī calls one route rare and al-Nasāʾī transmits it mursal, but Ibn Kathīr says the connected version is correct, supported by both Ṣaḥīḥ collections.
rows.anchor: وقال الترمذي: غريب من هذا الوجه. ورواه النسائي من حديث موسى

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: In another report, the Prophet tells Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, Ṣafiyya, and Fāṭima to seek salvation through God, since he cannot avail them, though they may ask him for his property.
rows.anchor: عن الأعرج، عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Yaʿlā reports from Abū Hurayra the warning to Banū Quṣayy, Hāshim, and ʿAbd Manāf: the Prophet is a warner, death will change things, and the Hour is appointed.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "يا بني قصي، يا بني هاشم

rows.speaker: قبيصة بن مخارق وزهير بن عمرو
rows.claim: Qubayṣa and Zuhayr report the Prophet's analogy: like a man who spots an enemy and urgently calls his family, he warned Banū ʿAbd Manāf of danger; Muslim and al-Nasāʾī transmit it.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عثمان عبد الرحمن بن مل النهدي، عن قبيصة وزهير بن عمرو الهلالي

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī reports that after gathering thirty relatives and sharing food and drink, the Prophet asked who would guarantee his debts and promises, join him in Paradise, and succeed him among his family; ʿAlī volunteered.
rows.anchor: عن عباد بن عبد الله الأسدي، عن علي، رضي الله عنه، قال: لما نزلت هذه الآية:

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: In a route Ibn Kathīr calls stranger and fuller, ʿAlī says the Prophet feared his clan's response and initially stayed silent; Gabriel warned that failure to obey would bring God's punishment.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، عن علي بن أبي طالب، رضي الله عنه، قال: لما نزلت هذه الآية

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī says he prepared a sheep, a measure of food, and milk for roughly forty Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib; everyone ate and drank their fill while the food and drink appeared untouched.
rows.anchor: قال علي، رضي الله عنه: فدعاني فقال: "يا علي، إن الله قد أمرني

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Abū Lahab twice interrupted the Prophet's first two gatherings by accusing him of sorcery; at the third, the Prophet said no Arab youth had brought his people better than his message of this world and the next.
rows.anchor: بدره أبو لهب إلى الكلام فقال: لهد ما سحركم صاحبكم. فتفرقوا ولم يكلمهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī's expanded version says ʿAlī alone offered to assist while youngest and physically unimpressive; the Prophet called him his brother and ordered the others to hear and obey him, prompting their laughter.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن الحارث، عن ابن عباس، عن علي بن أبي طالب، فذكر مثله، وزاد بعد قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr rejects this route's reliability: its sole transmitter in this form, ʿAbd al-Ghaffār Abū Maryam, was abandoned, a lying Shīʿī accused of fabricating reports and weakened by the imams.
rows.anchor: تفرد بهذا السياق عبد الغفار بن القاسم أبي مريم، وهو متروك كذاب شيعي، اتهمه علي بن المديني

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ibn Abī Ḥātim's version says the family repeatedly ate and drank their fill while little was depleted; after earlier interruptions, the Prophet asked who would settle his debts and succeed him among his family.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن الحارث قال: قال علي رضي الله عنه: لما نزلت هذه الآية:

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAbbās stayed silent fearing the burden on his wealth, while ʿAlī held back because of ʿAbbās's seniority; ʿAlī then volunteered, and the Prophet accepted him despite his self-described appearance.
rows.anchor: قال علي رضي الله عنه: لما نزلت هذه الآية: {وأنذر عشيرتك الأقربين}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet asked his uncles and cousins to cover his debts and look after his family because he feared being killed while bearing the burden of warning.
rows.anchor: ومعنى سؤاله، عليه الصلاة والسلام (7) لأعمامه وأولادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After 5:67 promised God's protection, the Prophet felt secure; he had previously been guarded until that verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: ولما أنزل الله عز وجل: {يا أيها الرسول بلغ ما أنزل إليك من ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr thinks the Prophet then publicly called at Ṣafā and warned Quraysh's clans, naming even close relatives to draw attention from the nearest to the broader audience.
rows.anchor: ثم كان بعد هذا -والله أعلم -دعاؤه الناس جهرة على الصفا، وإنذاره

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Abū al-Dardāʾ reports hearing the Prophet say that prophets are most detached from worldly life and their closest relatives are hardest on them; he adds that a scholar's family is least interested in his knowledge until he leaves.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الواحد الدمشقي قال: رأيت أبا الدرداء، رضي الله عنه، يحدث الناس ويفتيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rely on God in every affair: He supports, helps, protects, grants victory, and makes your word prevail.
rows.anchor: أي: في جميع أمورك؛ فإنه مؤيدك وناصرك وحافظك ومظفرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's seeing the Prophet when he rises means that God attends to and cares for him, as also expressed in 52:48.
rows.anchor: أي: هو معتن بك، كما قال تعالى: {واصبر (3) لحكم ربك فإنك بأعيننا}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the Prophet's rising as his rising to pray.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: {الذي يراك حين تقوم} يعني: إلى الصلاة.

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima says God sees the Prophet standing, bowing, and prostrating.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: يرى قيامه وركوعه وسجوده.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the phrase refers to the Prophet praying alone.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: {الذي يراك حين تقوم}

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk takes it to mean rising from the bed or from a sitting place.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: {الذي يراك حين تقوم.} أي: من فراشك أو مجلسك.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says God sees the Prophet standing, sitting, and in all his states.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: {الذي يراك} : قائما وجالسا وعلى حالاتك.

rows.speaker: قتادة، عكرمة، عطاء الخراساني، الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Qatāda, ʿIkrima, ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī, and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī interpret the Prophet's movement among prostrators as his prayer, seen both alone and in congregation.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: {الذي يراك حين تقوم. وتقلبك في الساجدين} قال: في الصلاة، يراك وحدك ويراك في الجمع.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the Prophet could see behind him as he saw in front; Ibn Kathīr supports this with the sound report, Align your rows, for I see you behind my back.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يرى من خلفه كما يرى من أمامه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report through two routes from Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the Prophet's movement as his transmission from one prophet's loins to another until God brought him forth as a prophet.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه قال في هذه الآية: يعني تقلبه من صلب نبي إلى صلب نبي،
